items.fullText: 이코노미 > IT 소방 전문 기업 'KMS', AI·IoT 기반 스마트 소방안전 신제품 2종 공개...스마트 방재 생태계 구축 나선다 발행일 : 2026-11-04 15:59 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 - 생활·산업 현장 아우르는 차세대 스마트 소방안전 플랫폼 구축 - 'SMART GAS FIRE SUPPRESSION MONITORING SYSTEM', 가스계소화설비 실시간 관제로 신뢰성 혁신 - 전국 대리점·유통·시공 파트너 모집 본격 확대 소방 전문 기업 'KMS', AI·IoT 기반 스마트 소방안전 신제품 2종 동시 공개 소방 전문기업 KMS(대표 김용한)가 인공지능(AI)·사물인터넷(IoT) 기술을 적용한 소공간 소화용구 '스마트 캔(SMART CAN)'과 산업용 '스마트 가스계소화설비 통합 모니터링 시스템(SMART GAS FIRE SUPPRESSION MONITORING SYSTEM)'을 공개했다고 밝혔다. 최근 소방안전 산업이 화재 진압뿐 아니라 실시간 위험 감지와 예방, 통합 관제 중심으로 확대되는 가운데 KMS는 전기 화재 대응과 산업용 소방설비 관리에 특화된 신제품 2종을 통해 스마트 소방안전 시장 공략에 나선다. SMART CAN, “소방안전을 선물한다”... 분배전반 화재 예방의 뉴 스탠다드 스마트 캔은 분배전반 내부와 전기설비 주변 소공간의 화재 대응에 특화된 AI·IoT 기반 소화용구다. '소방안전을 선물한다'는 모토로 개발됐으며, 화재 위험 징후를 사전에 감지하고 초기 단계에서 대응할 수 있도록 설계됐다. 제품명인 'SMART CAN'에는 △C(Compact): 분배전반 및 협소 공간에 적합한 소형 설계 △A(Automatic): AI·IoT 기반 자동 감지 및 대응 시스템 △N(Now): 화재 위험 발생 시 신속한 대응이라는 의미를 담았다. KMS는 스마트 캔 개발 과정에서 실제 화재 예방에 필요한 핵심 기능과 가격 경쟁력 확보에 집중했다. 이를 통해 전기 화재 대응 솔루션의 도입 부담을 낮추고 보급을 확대한다는 전략이다. 주요 기능으로는 분배전반 내부 온도와 습도를 실시간으로 감지해 과열 징후를 파악하는 '온·습도 센싱', 먼지 및 오염물 축적에 따른 전기 아크 발생 위험을 감지하는 '먼지(Dust) 센싱', 소화약제의 중량 변화를 확인하는 '소화약제 중량 모니터링' 등이 있다. 가스계설비 관제의 혁신, ‘SMART GAS FIRE SUPPRESSION MONITORING SYSTEM’ 함께 공개한 '스마트 가스계소화설비 통합 모니터링 시스템'은 대형 빌딩과 산업시설, 데이터센터 등에 설치되는 가스계소화설비를 실시간으로 통합 관리하는 플랫폼으로, KMS의 S-Link 주요 제품군에 해당한다. 가스계소화설비는 오작동이나 설비 이상이 발생할 경우 인명과 주요 시설의 안전에 영향을 줄 수 있어 지속적인 점검과 관리가 중요하다. 기존 현장에서는 인력 중심의 점검에 의존하는 경우가 많아 유지관리 효율성에 한계가 있었다. KMS는 자체 무선통신 기술과 고정밀 센서를 기반으로 설비 상태를 실시간으로 확인할 수 있도록 시스템을 구성했다. 주요 관제 항목은 △소화약제 실린더 압력 및 중량 상태 △기동용 가스 압력 △선택밸브 및 수동잠금밸브 개폐 상태 △전자솔레노이드 안전핀 체결 여부 △소화약제실 내 온도·습도·가스 농도 등이다. 특히 센서 개발부터 무선통신 장비 제작, 통합 관제 시스템 구축, 현장 시공까지 일괄 수행하는 턴키(Turn-key) 체계를 통해 산업 현장의 유지관리 효율성과 설비 운영 신뢰성을 높인다는 계획이다. 전국 파트너 네트워크 확대...스마트 방재 생태계 구축 본격화 KMS는 이번 신제품 2종 공개를 계기로 전국 단위 대리점과 유통·시공 파트너 모집도 확대한다. 개인 사업장의 소공간부터 대규모 산업 현장까지 적용 범위를 넓히고 스마트 소방안전 사업 기반을 강화할 방침이다. KMS 관계자는 “스마트 캔은 소방안전이 필요한 곳에 안전을 선물하겠다는 의지로 개발한 소공간 소화용

items.t: Data centers are turning to old jet engines as the wait for power grows
items.d: The years-long wait for access to the grid and new turbines is causing data center builders to turn to an unusual, less-efficient and less environmentally friendly solution: once-discarded jet engines.
items.fullText: Stuck in years-long lines for grid connections and new turbines, some AI data centers are making their own electricity with converted jet engines, the New York Times reported Tuesday. The engines, pulled from retired aircraft and rebuilt to burn natural gas, aren’t anyone’s idea of a permanent power plant. But they’re another sign of how far power supply has fallen behind the AI buildout. For companies stuck in those lines, the main draw of converted jet engines is how quickly the engines can be up and running. “It’s all about getting power as fast as possible,” Rystad Energy analyst Audun Martinsen told the Times. With jet-powered units, “they can have a data center running in 24 months,” he said. Hooking up 100 megawatts to the grid in Northern Virginia, by comparison, takes about seven years , according to the International Energy Agency. Most power capacity is expected to come on by 2031, an executive at Mitsubishi Power, one of the world’s top makers of power generation equipment, told Bloomberg last week . In some cases, these delays are already costing some data center operators business. Last month, Microsoft pulled out as the anchor customer for Nscale’s data center in Loughton, England, after the local utility said it couldn’t deliver enough power until the early to mid-2030s. Elon Musk’s xAI is among the companies already using the engines, having installed eight converted jet-engine turbines in Mississippi to help power its Colossus 2 data center in Memphis, the Times reported, citing state permits and satellite imagery. The units come from ProEnergy, which rebuilds a GE engine commonly found on Boeing jets. In 2025, OpenAI followed Musk’s lead with gas turbines at its first Stargate site in Abilene, Texas. items.t: AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges
items.d: The five-year-old startup raised a $1.3  billion round led by Bessemer.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 11:34 AM PST · November 3, 2026 Image Credits: monsitj / Getty Images Marina Temkin AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges Fal , a San Francisco-based startup that hosts and runs AI video, image, and audio models, has raised $1.3 billion in its latest funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price. The deal values Fal at $16 billion, double its $8 billion valuation in April, Bloomberg reported . The startup announced its Series E and F rounds at the same time, noting that a combined $1.65 billion was raised across both. (Sequoia led the earlier round.) The latest round (Series F) comes amid soaring demand for inference services, the process of running an AI model that’s already been trained to generate outputs, particularly from customers relying on open source models. Fal surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year, Bloomberg’s report noted. Companies providing inference services, including Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Modal, have also been growing rapidly and raising large funding rounds at higher valuations . But their gross margins remain thin because of the high cost of buying or leasing compute, according to several people familiar with inference companies’ financials. Fal was co-founded in 2021 by Burkay Gur, a former Coinbase machine learning leader and Oracle engineer, and Gorkem Yurtseven, who was previously a developer at Amazon. items.t: Google to shut off search for schools that opt out of AI
items.d: The company said AI-enabled products would be shut off by default for schools, which would also cut off their access to Google Search.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Google to shut off search for schools that opt out of AI The company said AI-enabled products would be shut off by default for schools, which would also cut off their access to Google Search. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Google headquarters in Mountain View, Calif. Justin Sullivan / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 3, 2026, 1:32 PM EST By Jared Perlo and Tyler Kingkade Google announced Tuesday morning that it would switch off AI products by default for students in schools that use the technology giant’s education software. But those schools that forgo its AI services would also be cut off from Google Search by default. The move comes after mounting criticism from advocacy groups and senators about the spread of Google’s AI services available in classrooms. Until Tuesday, its AI products — branded under the Gemini moniker — were automatically activated for schools using Google Classroom. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president and general manager of education, said in a blog post announcing the change that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search “will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.” “We believe schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach,” Phillips wrote. Later on Tuesday, after significant backlash to the announcement, Google said its policy would allow schools to enable the Search service alone, without turning on access to additional Gemini products. But schools would still not be able to use Search without certain AI features like AI-generated summaries, given AI’s growing integration into the company’s search functionality. items.t: Google will let schools disable its AI tools, but not without sacrificing Search
items.d: Schools choosing to restrict AI altogether will no longer be able to access Google Search, as AI features are now integrated into the search engine.
items.fullText: Google announced on Tuesday that it plans to disable AI tools for K-12 students next year unless school administrators explicitly turn them on. The tech giant says the change follows consultations with schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers. As a result, Google is revising its approach across Gemini, NotebookLM, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. The decision means that schools choosing to restrict AI altogether will no longer be able to access Google Search, as AI features are now integrated into the search engine. Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” which means that if a school chooses to restrict AI altogether, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” The change raises an issue for schools. Although teachers may not want students to use AI Overviews in Google Search to conduct research or complete assignments, they likely still want them to be able to have access to the search engine to find sources and other learning materials. However, Google Search and its AI features are now inseparable. Given the dominance of Google’s suite of apps in classrooms and the widespread use of Chromebooks, the decision underscores the company’s influence over the education sector. Schools that want to continue to have access to Google Search will have to accept its AI features. “We’ll share more specifics with schools in the coming months ahead of the changes rolling out so they have time to prepare and enable a smooth transition,” Phillips wrote in a blog post . “Our goal is simple: provide school leaders the control and confidence to use AI products in classrooms as they see fit.” Google announced the upcoming change alongside the launch of Guided Learning in schools. items.fullText: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It An AI-defined fab uses accelerated simulation, learned physics models and AI agents to give engineers faster answers across design, testing and manufacturing. November 3, 2026 by Timothy Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking. For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days. Physical experiments on a fab line are slow and expensive. A wrong call on yield or process quality has real consequences. AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast. Accelerated computing shortens simulation time, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before committing to physical trials. Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time. AI agents handle sequences of engineering tasks that once consumed hours. And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle. Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers. items.fullText: Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction October 21, 2026 by Niall Robinson 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Weather forecasts shape more than daily plans; timely weather information is crucial for energy producers, insurers and transport operators to plan around changing conditions. A global forecast can show a storm taking shape, but decisions about solar farms, shipping routes or insured property depend on what happens locally. NVIDIA Earth-2 gives developers and researchers a family of open AI models and tools they can customize with their own data. Running on NVIDIA computing, these technologies support global weather prediction, detailed regional forecasts and environmental research. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements StormScope EU is the latest model to join Earth-2 — a regional version of the StormScope model for short-term forecasting, trained over Europe weather and climate data. It uses EUMETSAT satellite observations to predict evolving cloud conditions across 16 Meteosat channels at 10-minute intervals. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing a live StormScope EU pipeline in an interactive weather demo built in partnership with Earthmover . The demo uses Earth2Studio to run forecasts and Earthmover’s data platform to manage and serve the real-time results, which are updated as soon as new satellite observations come in, every 10 minutes. Earthmover serves these results as map tiles, letting visitors explore predictions across Europe without downloading entire datasets. Developers can combine Earth-2 models in workflows tailored to regional needs, using StormScope for short-term forecasting and CorrDiff to add local detail to coarser weather data.
